title: Validation of the final version of a patient questionnaire to identify treatment-relevant upper limb spasticity movement disorder after stroke
summary:
The aim of this study is to develop a questionnaire tool that can be used to assess the risk of developing spasticity and to identify treatment-relevant spasticity in order to facilitate faster treatment and referral to specialist centres.
The aim of this study is to examine the agreement of  patients' self-assessment and clinical examination results carried out by the experts (gold standard).
The basis for this study are the results of a previous pilot study (multicentre
questionnaire study on the self-assessment of the severity of a spastic movement disorder after a stroke), in which three different questionnaires on the cardinal symptoms of spasticity (movement control impairment, muscle tone impairment and pain) were analysed. The questionnaire was developed on the basis of the available statistical results on comprehensibility, sensitivity and specificity as well as on the agreement between the self-assessment and the result of the medical examination. The same criteria are asked. The structure of the questionnaire was adapted and the wording of the questions was revised. All patients included complete the questionnaire and are then examined by an expert (physician). The agreement between the patient's self-assessment and the expert's assessment is then analysed. The aim of this study is to validate this final version of the patient questionnaire to identify a spastic movement disorder after stroke requiring treatment.

interventions.name: All patients receive a questionnaire to assess the severity of the three cardinal symptoms of a spastic movement disorder (stiffness of the affected joints, restriction of movement control, level of spasticity-associated pain).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Part 1
Patients with a first infarction of the middle cerebral artery (acute, subacute or chronic) or a Hemorrhage in the basal ganglia
Preserved capacity for insight and judgement
Adequate understanding of language and tasks, 
Attention span for 15 minutes

Part 2 
Additionally patients with cerebral or spinal cord injury (stroke, traumatic brain injury) or another chronic disease of the central nervous system (amyotrophic lateral sclerosis ALS, hereditary spastic spinal paralysis HSP, Parkinson's, MS, Alzheimer's) in their medical history.
Exclusion criteria:
Patients with other neurological diseases 
Reduced vigilance or attention span 
Patients with adult representation 
Patients with severe speech impairment
